title: The Successive Salvations: how the Lord's redemptive work proceeds through discrete stages
arc: The teaching enumerates the Lord's saving operation as a series of discrete stages, each performed by a distinct cosmological figure, by which the Light is progressively released from the powers of darkness, ordered, awakened, drawn down into flesh and raised again, and finally gathered home through the Call and Hearing in each soul.
reading:
This chapter sets out the full structure of redemption as a sequence of discrete savings. Despite the project title "Four Salvations," the surviving Coptic numbers them through to a fifth (ⲧⲙⲁϩⲧⲟⲩ), so the teaching is really the complete five-fold articulation of the Lord's saving work, where each stage is worked by a distinct named operation and addresses a distinct register of the captive Light.

The first salvation belongs to the First Man. At the time he went forth from the Greatness, the Light was rescued from the powers of darkness "within them" — that is, the divine influx descended into the realm of self-love itself and, working through the Living Spirit who came after him, broke the grip of the archonic host. This is the inmost saving moment: Divine Truth in its first descent seizes the captive light at the point where it had been engulfed, and a great immeasurable Light goes forth back into the aeons of the Greatness. Spiritually this is the original act by which the Lord enters the proprium-state and begins, in principle, to liberate every truth that self-love has swallowed.

The second salvation is that of the Living Spirit. Here the Father of Life with the Mother of Life "establish" — they set in order. Cosmoses of earth are constructed with their luminaries, and the great immeasurable Light is rescued from the hands of the archons who had swallowed the First Man. Where the first salvation was the descent and seizing, this second is the building of structure: the operative Divine power constructs the heavenly framework in which the captured light can be safely held and refined. In the regenerate human this corresponds to the Lord's work of establishing ordered states in the natural mind so that what was swallowed by the proprium can begin to be sorted out.

The third salvation belongs to the Third Ambassador. He "reveals forth" his image before the archonic host, manifesting his likeness of light. This is the awakening call: revealed truth shown as a visible icon at the boundary between the heavens and the worlds of darkness, by which what is mingled in those powers is drawn upward. Where the Living Spirit built the framework, the Ambassador shows the form that calls the trapped light to recognize itself.

The fourth salvation, and the one given the fullest treatment, is that of Jesus the Radiance. When he reveals himself in the Zone, he shows his image before the firmaments and "chooses out" the light which is in the upper place — the sorting, by his shining, of what stands in the heavens above the firmaments. He establishes the arch-[ons in their proper bondage], takes a likeness, and likens himself to the angels until he reaches the lower stations. Then he descends all the way to the molding of the flesh, sets the lands and all the mountains in their proper order, and once again raises the immeasurable Light throughout the whole Building. He establishes the Call and the Hearing in the very elements, forms Jesus the Youth — the inner Christ-form in the regenerate soul — and then ascends and rests in the Land of Light. This is the complete saving arc taken in one figure: descent through every degree, accommodation even to flesh, the planting of the Call and its Hearing into the natural substance, the forming of the inner Radiance as a stable presence, and the return upward. In correspondence: the Lord glorifies his Human, and in doing so makes the whole vertical column of redemption operative within the regenerate.

The fifth salvation is the release-forth of the Great Counsel, which is identified with the Call and the Hearing themselves, working as one. This is the saving of the soul out from [the dwelling] of the Greatness — that is, the application of the previous four to the actual soul in its journey. The fragmentary middle of this section enumerates further inner aspects (a fourth and a fifth treated again in compressed form), and speaks of being drawn "inward unto him, before his face, of his image of Light, in this Panaretos" — the All-Virtuous one, the consummating likeness in which redeemed souls are gathered. The end of the teaching describes how the souls came forth from the first place, look again unto the Light, and go up to him at the end, upward "from the beginning unto" the consummation. The fifth salvation is therefore not a new event alongside the others but the ongoing operation by which the work done by the First Man, the Living Spirit, the Ambassador, and Jesus the Radiance becomes effective in each soul through the Call answered by Hearing, until the final gathering.

Read as one spiritual argument, the teaching presents redemption as a process through discrete degrees rather than a single act. The Lord's saving works are distinguished according to where in the cosmic-human structure they operate: at the inmost descent into self-love (First Man), at the building of order in the natural (Living Spirit), at the awakening manifestation across the firmament-boundary (Third Ambassador), at the full glorification through flesh and the planting of the Call in the elements (Jesus the Radiance), and at the responsive uptake of that Call by individual souls drawn into the final image (Great Counsel / Panaretos). Each stage is necessary; each works upon what the previous has prepared; together they trace the complete column of ascent by which all light, having been seized, ordered, revealed, embodied, and called, returns home to the Land of Light.
